slides.title: prompt mistakes that make AI sound **robotic**.
slides.sub: And the one-line fix for each. Tested on the same customer reply, before and after.

messages.text: Write a reply to a customer whose order is late.

Dear Valued Customer,
Thank you for reaching out. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused by the delay of your order. Please rest assured that we are working diligently to resolve this matter. Your satisfaction is our top priority...

slides.note: Nothing wrong with it. Nobody would ever believe a person wrote it.

steps.d: Fix: 'I run a small candle shop and I write casually.'
Fix: paste 2–3 lines you actually wrote to a customer.
Fix: 'She's a regular, a little annoyed, reading on her phone.'
It tends to come back stiff. Describe the tone: 'like a text to a regular.'
Fix: 'Don't use: valued customer, any inconvenience, rest assured.'
Fix: reply 'shorter, warmer, cut the last line.'

cards.title: Late-order reply
cards.text: I run [BUSINESS]. Write a reply to [NAME], a regular whose order is late. Facts: [WHAT HAPPENED + NEW DATE]. Sound like me: [PASTE 2–3 LINES YOU WROTE]. Friendly and plain, like a text to a regular. Under 80 words. Don't use: 'valued customer', 'any inconvenience', 'rest assured'.

slides.note: Leave out order numbers, addresses and other private details.

before.label: ONE-LINE PROMPT
before.text: Dear Valued Customer, thank you for reaching out. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused by the delay of your order...

after.label: WITH THE 7 FIXES
after.text:
Hi Jess, I'm so sorry, your order is running late. Our wax delivery came in behind schedule, so we're a few days behind on pouring. Your candles ship Thursday and I'll send tracking the minute they do. Thanks for hanging in there!
— Sam

slides.note: Example candle shop and names, invented.

items.d: Copy them from a real message you sent.
'Like a text to a regular', not 'professional'.
Then ask for one round of edits.

slides.after: I'll DM you **21 more prompts** for sales, bookings, money and your team. Free, for followers.

caption:
How to make AI replies sound less robotic: 7 prompt mistakes and the fix for each

I asked for the same late-order reply twice. The one-line prompt gave me "Dear Valued Customer... rest assured...". The fixed prompt gave me something a real shop owner would send.

The 7 mistakes: no context about you, no sample of your voice, no reader, asking for "professional", no length limit, no banned phrases, keeping the first draft.

Copy this:

"I run [BUSINESS]. Write a reply to [NAME], a regular whose order is late. Facts: [WHAT HAPPENED + NEW DATE]. Sound like me: [PASTE 2–3 LINES YOU WROTE]. Friendly and plain, like a text to a regular. Under 80 words. Don't use: 'valued customer', 'any inconvenience', 'rest assured'."

Leave out order numbers and addresses. Then reply "shorter, warmer" once before you send.
